Borrowed from Jewish Babylonian Aramaic אגב (ʾaggaḇ, literally “on the back [of]”), from earlier Aramaic עַל גַּב (ʿal gaḇ).

Borrowed from Jewish Babylonian Aramaic אַלִּיבָּא (ʾallibbā, “according to, (lit.) on the heart [of]”).
Action noun of אִלְתֵּר (iltér, “to improvise”), itself denominated from אַלְתַּר (“immediately”), itself from Jewish Babylonian Aramaic אַלְתַּר (“immediately”). Doublet of אֲתָר (atár, “a site”).

parole.significato: bless you, gesundheit (response to someone sneezing)
parole.testo: From Jewish Babylonian Aramaic אָסוּתָא (ʾāsūṯā, “cure, remedy”).
From ב־ (b'-) + דיעבד (di'avád), which is from Jewish Babylonian Aramaic [Term?] a compound of דְּאִי (dʾy) + עֲבַד (ʿvd), meaning if done.

parole.significato: in the absence of, in the case where ... is not found, when lacking, if there is not
parole.testo: From Jewish Babylonian Aramaic בִּדְלֵיכָּא (biḏlēḵā), from Aramaic בִּ־ (bi-, “in [the case]”) + Aramaic דְ־ (ḏ-, “that”) + Aramaic לֵיכָּא (lēḵā, “there is not”).
Abbreviation of Jewish Babylonian Aramaic בסיעתא דשמיא (“with the help of Heaven”)
From Jewish Babylonian Aramaic בעיא (“dilemma, something that needs to be worked out”), from the root ב־ע־י (“to request, to need”).
From Jewish Babylonian Aramaic בר אווזא, equivalent to בַּר (bár, “son of”) + אֲוָז (aváz, “goose”).

From ברווז / בַּרְוָז (barváz, “a duck”) + ־וֹן (-on, suffix forming diminutives), the first part from Jewish Babylonian Aramaic בר אווזא, equivalent to בַּר (bár, “son of”) + אווז / אֲוָז (aváz, “goose”).

parole.significato: a dead man, one who is almost dead, one who is considered dead
parole.testo: Borrowed from Jewish Babylonian Aramaic גַּבְרָא קְטִילָא (gaḇrā qəṭīlā, “(lit.) killed man”)

parole.significato: that is, which means, in other words
parole.testo: Borrowed from Jewish Babylonian Aramaic היינו (hāynū, “behold”), from Aramaic הָדֵין הוּא (hāḏēn hū, “which this is”).
From Jewish Babylonian Aramaic כְּסִפְתָּא.

Borrowed from Jewish Babylonian Aramaic לכאורה (“at first glance”). The word appears only once in the Talmud. Common in the language of the Rishonim and Acharonim.

parole.significato: brass (a metallic alloy of copper and zinc used in many industrial and plumbing applications)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Jewish Babylonian Aramaic פְּלִיזָא (pəlizzā). Compare Arabic فِلِزّ (filizz, “brass”) and Classical Syriac ܦܠܸܙܵܐ (pəlezzā).
